command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
[ -f "$change/proposal.md" ] || { echo "$record names change '$change_name', but $change/proposal.md does not exist - write the change there, or name the active change the task is about"; exit 1; }
verdict=$(sed -n 's/^Verdict:[[:space:]]*//p' "$record" | head -1)
if [ "$verdict" != "no-blocking-dependencies" ]; then
  echo "the change record's verdict is '$verdict'; the only verdict that finishes this stage is 'no-blocking-dependencies'."
  echo "If the change IS blocked, do not finish the round: write the dependency chain to the path in \$GNOMISH_DECISION_FILE as {\"question\": \"...\", \"options\": [\"...\"]}, delete $record and end your turn."
  exit 1
fi

findings.message: grid-view delta contradicts an unmodified requirement: FR8/D7 make a dragged handle keep its press offset ('the handle's end goes to the position of the handle at the press, plus the pointer's horizontal travel since the press'), with a press up to 22 px from the grip centre inside the new 44 px hit area. The unchanged requirement 'Handle drag scrolls the strips' in openspec/specs/grid-view/spec.md:364 still says the handle's end 'stays the track step under the pointer', and its scenarios say 'the end handle stays within one track step of the finger' (lines 371, 378). On a phone a track step is ~1/4 of a cell pitch (~10-12 px), so the two requirements conflict. The delta must MODIFY 'Handle drag scrolls the strips' (and its scenarios) to the grab-offset rule.

tasks.md ordering defect: task 3.2 removes MeetingRangeInputOutcome.INVALID_RANGE from src/controller/useMeetingRange.ts and requires that `grep -rn "INVALID_RANGE" src` (test files included) prints nothing. But src/views/shared/MeetingRangeInput.tsx:81-87, MeetingRangeInput.test.tsx:155,186 and LocalDateTime.meetingInput.test.tsx:83 still reference INVALID_RANGE until task 4.2 changes them. Task 3.2 therefore cannot be verified (the grep fails and those files no longer compile) when it runs. Move the grep, or the view and test updates, so each task is independently verifiable in order.

Glossary synonym: the spec and design call the bar 'the date bar' (glossary docs/glossary/date-selection.md: '**Date bar** — the bar at the bottom of the main page … *Code:* `DateBar`'), yet design D5 and tasks 4.4/5.1 name its new locator `data-page-bar` / `PAGE_BAR_SELECTOR`. 'Page bar' is not a glossary term, and no entry is added. .claude/rules/glossary.md: 'A name that carries a glossary concept under a different word is a bug, even if the code works.' Use a date-bar name (e.g. `data-date-bar` / `DATE_BAR_SELECTOR`), or add a glossary entry for the page bar as a distinct concept and list it in proposal 'What Changes'.
